paragraphs.text: Καὶ μεθ' ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ' ἰδίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai meth' hēmeras hex paralambanei ho Iēsous ton Petron kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn ton adelphon autou, kai anapherei autous eis oros hypsēlon kat' idian.

i18n.en: And after six days Jesus took with him Peter and James and John his brother, and led them up onto a high mountain by themselves.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Transfiguration narrative opens.** *Kai meth' hēmeras hex paralambanei ho Iēsous ton Petron kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn ... kai anaferei autous eis oros hypsēlon kat' idian* — 'after six days, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John ... and brings them up to a high mountain by themselves'. The 'high mountain' (*oros hypsēlon*) traditionally identified as Mt Tabor (Origen onward) but more recently as Mt Hermon (2,814m, near Caesarea Philippi where Mt 16 sets the prior episode) per France NICNT 645. The mountain-as-revelation-site pattern continues from Mt 5:1 (SM) toward Mt 28:16 (Great Commission). See `transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals` and `mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς.
paragraphs.translit: kai metemorphōthē emprosthen autōn, kai elampsen to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios, ta de himatia autou egeneto leuka hōs to phōs.

i18n.en: And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his garments became white as the light.

paragraphs.commentary: *kai metemorphōthē emprosthen autōn, kai elampsen to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios, ta de himatia autou egeneto leuka hōs to phōs* — 'and he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as the light'. The passive *metemorphōthē* preserves the divine-passive (the transfiguration is something done-to Jesus, not by him). The luminous-face-shining echoes Ex 34:29-35 (Moses' shining face after speaking with YHWH); the luminous-figure cross-corpus to Dan 10:6 LXX (the man-in-linen vision) and 1 Enoch 14:18-22 (the luminous-throne theophany). One of the three major Raëlian-canon engagement sites — acknowledgment-without-endorsement applied. See `transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας συλλαλοῦντες μετ' αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou ōphthē autois Mōusēs kai Ēlias syllalountes met' autou.

i18n.en: And behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elijah, talking with him.

paragraphs.commentary: *Mōysēs kai Hēlias syllalountes met' autou* — 'Moses and Elijah talking with him'. Three readings of the Moses-Elijah pairing: (a) Law/Prophets witness-pair (mainstream Christian-tradition); (b) eschatological-returning figures (Moses-redivivus per Deut 18:15; Elijah-redivivus per Mal 4:5-6 + Mt 11:14); (c) bodily-translated figures (Moses' divinely-buried at Deut 34:5-6 + Assumption of Moses tradition; Elijah's 2 Kgs 2:11 fiery-chariot translation). Davies-Allison ICC 2.696-697.

paragraphs.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι· εἰ θέλεις, ποιήσω ὧδε τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Petros eipen tō Iēsou· Kyrie, kalon estin hēmas hōde einai· ei theleis, poiēsō hōde treis skēnas, soi mian kai Mōusei mian kai Ēlia mian.

i18n.en: And Peter answered and said to Jesus: "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, I will make here three tents: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."

paragraphs.commentary: Peter proposes three *skēnas* (tents/booths). Cross-corpus possibly to the Feast of Tabernacles / Sukkot (Lev 23:42-43) eschatological-dwelling tradition, or to the Ex 25:8-9 Tabernacle-pattern revealed on the mountain.

paragraphs.text: ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ νεφέλη φωτεινὴ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα· ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: eti autou lalountos idou nephelē phōteinē epeskiasen autous, kai idou phōnē ek tēs nephelēs legousa· Houtos estin ho huios mou ho agapētos, en hō eudokēsa· akouete autou.

i18n.en: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud, saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him."

paragraphs.commentary: **Four-layered scriptural-allusion in the bath-qol voice.** *houtos estin ho huios mou ho agapētos, en hō eudokēsa; akouete autou* — the divine-voice declaration combines: (i) Ps 2:7 LXX *huios mou ei sy* (Davidic-royal enthronement-psalm); (ii) Isa 42:1 LXX *ho agapētos mou en hō eudokēsen hē psychē mou* (Servant-of-YHWH first-servant-song); (iii) Deut 18:15 *autou akousesthe* (prophet-like-Moses prediction); (iv) Mt 3:17 baptism-voice intratextual-echo. The four-layered allusion compresses Davidic-messianic + Servant-figure + prophet-like-Moses + intratextual significations. The *nephelē phōteinē* (bright cloud) echoes Ex 24:15-18 Sinai-cloud-glory. See `transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα.
paragraphs.translit: kai akousantes hoi mathētai epesan epi prosōpon autōn kai ephobēthēsan sphodra.

i18n.en: And when the disciples heard, they fell on their faces and were exceedingly afraid.

paragraphs.text: καὶ προσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἁψάμενος αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
paragraphs.translit: kai prosēlthen ho Iēsous kai hapsamenos autōn eipen· Egerthēte kai mē phobeisthe.

i18n.en: And Jesus came and touched them, saying: "Rise up, and do not be afraid."

paragraphs.text: ἐπάραντες δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν οὐδένα εἶδον εἰ μὴ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον.
paragraphs.translit: eparantes de tous ophthalmous autōn oudena eidon ei mē auton Iēsoun monon.

i18n.en: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus himself alone.

paragraphs.text: καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα ἕως οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθῇ.
paragraphs.translit: kai katabainontōn autōn ek tou orous eneteilato autois ho Iēsous legōn· Mēdeni eipēte to horama heōs hou ho huios tou anthrōpou ek nekrōn egerthē.

i18n.en: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: "Tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man is raised from the dead."

paragraphs.commentary: *tō huiō tou anthrōpou ek nekrōn egerthē* — the Son-of-Man resurrection-prediction. The messianic-secret pattern: the disciples are commanded not-to-speak-of-the-vision until after the resurrection. See `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Τί οὖν οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōtēsan auton hoi mathētai legontes· Ti oun hoi grammateis legousin hoti Ēlian dei elthein prōton;

i18n.en: And his disciples asked him, saying: "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"

paragraphs.commentary: Disciples' question about Elijah's coming. The Mal 4:5-6 Elijah-redivivus expectation; Mt 11:14 explicitly identifies the Baptist with Elijah-redivivus. Davies-Allison ICC 2.711-715.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἠλίας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα·
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ēlias men erchetai kai apokatastēsei panta·

i18n.en: And he answered and said: "Elijah indeed is coming and will restore all things;

paragraphs.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἠλίας ἤδη ἦλθεν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτὸν ἀλλὰ ἐποίησαν ἐν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν· οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει πάσχειν ὑπ' αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legō de hymin hoti Ēlias ēdē ēlthen, kai ouk epegnōsan auton alla epoiēsan en autō hosa ēthelēsan· houtōs kai ho huios tou anthrōpou mellei paschein hyp' autōn.

i18n.en: but I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished; so also the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands."

paragraphs.commentary: *Hēlias ēdē ēlthen* — Jesus identifies Elijah-already-come (the Baptist). The Son-of-Man passion-prediction integrated with the Elijah-typology. See `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: tote synēkan hoi mathētai hoti peri Iōannou tou baptistou eipen autois.

i18n.en: Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντων πρὸς τὸν ὄχλον προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπος γονυπετῶν αὐτὸν
paragraphs.translit: Kai elthontōn pros ton ochlon prosēlthen autō anthrōpos gonypetōn auton

i18n.en: And when they came to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling before him,

paragraphs.commentary: The demoniac-boy pericope opens. Synoptic-parallel: Mk 9:14-29; Lk 9:37-43. The Matthean form is shorter than the Markan.

paragraphs.text: καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐλέησόν μου τὸν υἱόν, ὅτι σεληνιάζεται καὶ κακῶς πάσχει· πολλάκις γὰρ πίπτει εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ πολλάκις εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ.
paragraphs.translit: kai legōn· Kyrie, eleēson mou ton huion, hoti selēniazetai kai kakōs paschei· pollakis gar piptei eis to pyr kai pollakis eis to hydōr.

i18n.en: and saying: "Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is moon-struck and suffers grievously; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.

paragraphs.commentary: *selēniazetai* — 'is moonstruck' (literally lunatic-from-Selēnē 'moon'). The ancient diagnosis of epilepsy / seizure-disorders attributed to lunar-influence. The Matthean term (vs the Markan *pneuma alalon* 'mute spirit') reflects different ancient medical-categories.

paragraphs.text: καὶ προσήνεγκα αὐτὸν τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν αὐτὸν θεραπεῦσαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai prosēnegka auton tois mathētais sou, kai ouk ēdynēthēsan auton therapeusai.

i18n.en: And I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him."

paragraphs.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε μεθ' ὑμῶν ἔσομαι; ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; φέρετέ μοι αὐτὸν ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen· Ō genea apistos kai diestrammenē, heōs pote meth' hymōn esomai; heōs pote anexomai hymōn; pherete moi auton hōde.

i18n.en: And Jesus answered and said: "O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to me."

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τὸ δαιμόνιον· καὶ ἐθεραπεύθη ὁ παῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
paragraphs.translit: kai epetimēsen autō ho Iēsous, kai exēlthen ap' autou to daimonion· kai etherapeuthē ho pais apo tēs hōras ekeinēs.

i18n.en: And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him; and the boy was healed from that hour.

paragraphs.text: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ κατ' ἰδίαν εἶπον· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
paragraphs.translit: Tote proselthontes hoi mathētai tō Iēsou kat' idian eipon· Dia ti hēmeis ouk ēdynēthēmen ekbalein auto;

i18n.en: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said: "Why could we not cast it out?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τὴν ὀλιγοπιστίαν ὑμῶν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Μετάβα ἔνθεν ἐκεῖ, καὶ μεταβήσεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de legei autois· Dia tēn oligopistian hymōn· amēn gar legō hymin, ean echēte pistin hōs kokkon sinapeōs, ereite tō orei toutō· Metaba enthen ekei, kai metabēsetai, kai ouden adynatēsei hymin.

i18n.en: And he said to them: "Because of your little faith. For amen I say to you, if you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.

paragraphs.commentary: *ean echēte pistin hōs kokkon sinapeōs ... ereite tō orei toutō, metaba enthen ekei, kai metabēsetai* — the mustard-seed-faith + move-the-mountain saying. Cross-synoptic Mt 21:21; Mk 11:23; 1 Cor 13:2. The mountain-imagery may activate the Matthean revelation-mountain pattern. See `mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu`.

paragraphs.text: [Τοῦτο δὲ τὸ γένος οὐκ ἐκπορεύεται εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ καὶ νηστείᾳ.]
paragraphs.translit: [Touto de to genos ouk ekporeuetai ei mē en proseuchē kai nēsteia.]

i18n.en: [But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.]

paragraphs.text: Συστρεφομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μέλλει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων,
paragraphs.translit: Systrephomenōn de autōn en tē Galilaia eipen autois ho Iēsous· Mellei ho huios tou anthrōpou paradidosthai eis cheiras anthrōpōn,

i18n.en: And as they were gathering together in Galilee, Jesus said to them: "The Son of Man is about to be handed over into the hands of men,

paragraphs.commentary: **Second passion-prediction.** *mellei ho huios tou anthrōpou paradidosthai eis cheiras anthrōpōn* — 'the Son of Man is about to be handed over into human hands'. Part of the threefold Matthean passion-prediction series (Mt 16:21; 17:22-23; 20:18-19). The wordplay *huios tou anthrōpou ... eis cheiras anthrōpōn* (Son of Man into human hands) is preserved in Greek. See `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται. καὶ ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα.
paragraphs.translit: kai apoktenousin auton, kai tē tritē hēmera egerthēsetai. kai elypēthēsan sphodra.

i18n.en: and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised." And they were exceedingly grieved.

paragraphs.text: Ἐλθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθον οἱ τὰ δίδραχμα λαμβάνοντες τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν οὐ τελεῖ τὰ δίδραχμα;
paragraphs.translit: Elthontōn de autōn eis Kapharnaoum prosēlthon hoi ta didrachma lambanontes tō Petrō kai eipan· Ho didaskalos hymōn ou telei ta didrachma;

i18n.en: And when they came to Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and said: "Does not your teacher pay the two-drachma tax?"

paragraphs.commentary: **The temple-tax pericope** (vv.24-27). The *didrachma* — the two-drachma annual Temple-tax (Ex 30:11-16 the half-shekel atonement-tax tradition). The Matthean Jesus engages with the tax in a complex theological-political way: free-from-tax-as-sons but pays-it-not-to-offend. Uniquely Matthean.

paragraphs.text: λέγει· Ναί. καὶ ἐλθόντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προέφθασεν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Τί σοι δοκεῖ, Σίμων; οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τίνων λαμβάνουσιν τέλη ἢ κῆνσον; ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων;
paragraphs.translit: legei· Nai. kai elthonta eis tēn oikian proephthasen auton ho Iēsous legōn· Ti soi dokei, Simōn; hoi basileis tēs gēs apo tinōn lambanousin telē ē kēnson; apo tōn huiōn autōn ē apo tōn allotriōn;

i18n.en: He said, "Yes." And when he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: "What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take tolls or tribute? From their own sons, or from strangers?"

paragraphs.text: εἰπόντος δέ· Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων, ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρα γε ἐλεύθεροί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοί.
paragraphs.translit: eipontos de· Apo tōn allotriōn, ephē autō ho Iēsous· Ara ge eleutheroi eisin hoi huioi.

i18n.en: And when he said, "From strangers," Jesus said to him: "Then the sons are free.

paragraphs.text: ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς, πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα· ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hina de mē skandalisōmen autous, poreutheis eis thalassan bale ankistron kai ton anabanta prōton ichthyn aron, kai anoixas to stoma autou heurēseis statēra· ekeinon labōn dos autois anti emou kai sou.

i18n.en: But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and when you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater. Take that and give it to them for me and yourself."

paragraphs.commentary: *stater* — a four-drachma coin found in the fish's mouth. The fish-coin episode has been read as: (a) literal-miracle of provision; (b) parable-symbolic action; (c) folk-tale type. Davies-Allison ICC 2.745-746.
